title: Research audit: preserve route width through binary/radix conversion
body:
PR2972 leaves the routing-call width connection open. For PR2157's fixed-header route reduction, this audit proves that the binary-padded call converts back to a radix-q ordinary callee of exactly the original width w, on volume q²V. It connects these actual call widths to the twelve inherited stopped-range comparisons. The selected κ is unchanged.

The contribution is `research/qadic-route-cutoff-audit/`: an all-width arithmetic/padding proof, exact source pins, a complete replay receipt and an independent forward-address oracle. It adds only this isolated research package.

Base: `463113d675af7410ac91d53a4fed51ec6494eb9a`. OS assignment seed 73, adversarial mathematical audit. PR2157 is pinned at `eb1bf93950e9b14f7fadca7892866e9f29a26ad3`; PR2972 at `d6b883f97d2fd176171553b695005a132156d961`. The live inputs are pinned by Git blob and SHA-256 in SOURCES.json.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qadic-route-cutoff-audit
```

Passed locally on CPython 3.12.14/Linux: 48 complete actual-router packets, four full conversion roundtrips, twelve inherited cutoff comparisons, eight semantic controls and five failure-boundary tests, including optimized Python. The selected-record check also passes. Small-q fixtures exercise the source algebra outside the selected q>2^80 domain; the written proof covers that domain. Clean-export verification is recorded in the handoff.

Scope: the innermost completed ordinary endpoint is an explicit oracle. This does not derive an actual stock coefficient, implement a physical callee, validate the all-size compiler, admit a supplier or prove the full multiplication theorem. The q² cost depends on the fixed radix. PR2972's cutoff arithmetic and PR2547's conditional reserve reuse are predecessor work, not claimed as new.

Credit Jose Manuel/PR2157, Hiroki KUMAZAKI/PR2972, ToikY/PR1990, Josie Elliston/PR1956/1965, the retained PR185/PR387 cover/conversion lineage, Nick Petalas's PR2140 carry work and the existing BIT supplier/hosting authors. Prepared for Sricharan Vagvala (@theon199) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed.
